venue.name: Museum at Campbell River
venue.description: The Museum at Campbell River holds historic and ethnographic collections from northern Vancouver Island, with galleries on First Nations history, logging, fishing and settlement, plus outdoor exhibits including the restored fishing boat Soyokaze. It runs guided education programs for grades K to 12 at a flat fee per class, and a cheaper unguided class visit with clipboard activities. The building is at 470 Island Highway with free parking, washrooms and a picnic area, and the museum also looks after the Haig-Brown property. Admission is charged and children aged 5 and under are free.
venue.address: 470 Island Hwy, Campbell River, BC V9W 4Z9

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Accessible for the disabled. Courtesy wheelchair available

restrictions: Photographs are not allowed in the First Nations Gallery
venue.hours_notes: Summer, May 18 to Sept 30, daily 10am to 5pm. Winter, Oct 1 to May 17, Tuesday to Sunday 12pm to 5pm. December, Dec 1 to Dec 31, daily 10am to 5pm. Closed Good Friday, Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day.
venue.seasonal_notes: Two programs run only at set times of year. Bark, Roots & Berries runs April to August, and Christmas Past runs in December.
venue.price_year_or_season: School program fees are posted for the 2025-2026 school year

programs.name: First Nations of Northern Vancouver Island
programs.description: A two hour guided program on the three linguistic and cultural First Nations groups of northern Vancouver Island, the Kwakwaka'wakw, Coast Salish and Nuu-chah-nulth, and on the artistic styles in their crests. The museum says it can be adapted for any grade level and that it also runs by video conferencing for classes at a distance.
programs.what_children_do: Take an interactive tour of the First Nations Gallery, then make their own paint from ochre and salmon eggs.
programs.our_note: This is the only one of their programs that runs the whole way from kindergarten to grade 12, so it is the safest pick if you are unsure what will land with your group. Say your grade in the request form and ask how they pitch it.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: The Museum at Campbell River offers a variety of educational programs for grades K to 12

programs.name: Bark, Roots & Berries
programs.description: A two hour program in the museum's West Coast Garden and First Nations Gallery about the native plants of northern Vancouver Island and how local First Nations cultivate and harvest them. It runs April to August only. Most of it is outdoors, and the museum warns that the gravel trail around the building has a steep grade that may not suit some wheelchairs in wet weather.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the garden trail looking at native plants, examine the materials used in tools and regalia in the gallery, then make compostable pots and plant seeds to take home.
programs.our_note: Most of this one is outside on a gravel trail with a steep grade, so bring rain gear and raise the wheelchair question early if you need to. The April to August window is the tight end of the school year, so book well ahead.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building itself is wheelchair accessible. Part of this one is outside and there is nothing published about a wet weather plan, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: This program is offered from April to August when the flowers and berries are most visible.

programs.name: Grease Trails & Otter Tales
programs.description: A two hour program on the Pacific fur trade and its short and long term effects on northern Vancouver Island, using the First Nations and Transitions Galleries. Thirty minutes of it is outdoors.
programs.what_children_do: Look at coastal trade networks in two galleries, then take the part of European fur traders and use leadlines to chart the ocean floor.
programs.our_note: Half an hour of this is outside whatever the weather, so dress the group for it. The grade band is wide, so tell them where your class actually sits when you request it.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building itself is wheelchair accessible. Part of this one is outside and there is nothing published about a wet weather plan, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: This 2-hour program includes 30 minutes of outdoor activity.

programs.name: Unsinkable: The Soyokaze Story
programs.description: A two hour program on the experiences of Japanese Canadians during the Second World War, told through local families, with a tour on board the restored cod fishing boat Soyokaze. Thirty minutes is outdoors, and the museum cannot board the boat in ice or heavy rain.
programs.what_children_do: Go aboard a restored wooden fishing boat, then practise origami and try writing with a Japanese phonetic alphabet.
programs.our_note: The boat is the part children remember, and it is also the part they lose in bad weather. If the forecast is icy or wet, ask what happens to that half hour before you get on the bus.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building itself is wheelchair accessible. Part of this one is outside and there is nothing published about a wet weather plan, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: This 2-hour program includes 30 minutes of outdoor activity.

programs.name: Stones, Bones & Middens
programs.description: A two hour program on the earliest history of the Pacific Northwest Coast and the methods archaeologists use, with hands on work using locally found artifacts. Thirty minutes is outdoors.
programs.what_children_do: Handle artifacts found locally, then make their own stone tools using the same techniques First Peoples used on this coast.
programs.our_note: Making a stone tool is the draw here, and it needs enough adults to supervise properly. Their own pages disagree on whether grade 6 can come, so settle that first.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building itself is wheelchair accessible. Part of this one is outside and there is nothing published about a wet weather plan, so ask when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: This 2-hour program includes 30 minutes of outdoor activity.

programs.name: Impacts of Colonization
programs.description: A two hour program on the short and long term impacts of colonization on the First Nations of northern Vancouver Island, built around a guided discussion. The museum says it works best as a review after classroom study rather than as an introduction to the topic.
programs.what_children_do: Look critically at how the museum's own exhibits tell this story, take part in a guided discussion, then make a personal Reconciliation Reminder to take home.
programs.our_note: They say plainly that this works as a review, not an introduction, so it needs groundwork in class first. Their two pages give different grade ranges, so check yours is in.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: This 2-hour program examines some of the short and long-term impacts of colonization

programs.name: Haig-Brown Property Guided Tour
programs.description: A guided tour of the Haig-Brown property covering the life and work of Roderick Haig-Brown, including his study. Most of the tour is outdoors. The museum's booking form lists it as one hour, while the program sheet describes a two hour program.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the grounds of the Haig-Brown property and go inside the study where he wrote his books and articles.
programs.our_note: This one is not at the museum building, it is at the Haig-Brown property, so plan the bus for a second address. They give two different lengths for it, so ask which you are getting.
programs.practical_summary: Most of this is outdoors at a separate property, and nothing is published about washrooms, lunch space or a wet weather plan there. Ask about all three when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.

programs.name: Christmas Past
programs.description: A one hour seasonal program on winter holiday traditions in the community, with a puppet show about the wreck of the Northwestern and carolling through an imaginary forest. The museum invites classes to bring handmade ornaments for the Kindertree in its Festival of Trees. The booking form gave dates of 1 to 16 December 2025.
programs.what_children_do: Watch a puppet show, carol through an imaginary forest, make an autograph book to take home and hang a handmade ornament on a tree in a settler cabin.
programs.our_note: An hour is short enough for kindergarten and grade 1, which is rare here. The museum says it fills quickly and the only dates published had already passed, so ring early to get on the December list.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: this 1-hour festive program offers students a fun introduction to the Museum

programs.name: Letters From The Front: Archival Research
programs.description: An hour and a half archival research program for grades 9 to 12. It appears only on the museum's booking request form, and there is no description of it on the education programs page or a program sheet.
programs.our_note: This one is only listed on their booking form, with no description anywhere, so ask what it actually involves before you choose it over a program you can read about.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: Letters From The Front: Archival Research (Grades 9-12) - 1.5-hrs

programs.name: Unguided Museum Visit
programs.description: A self guided visit for a class at $60 per class for up to 30 students, with four themed clipboard activities on storytelling, tools, exhibits and artifacts included in the fee. Teachers can use their own worksheets instead and still borrow the museum's clipboards and pencils. The museum says this rate is only available to K to 12 groups.
programs.what_children_do: Move through the galleries at their own pace with a clipboard, working through a themed activity or a worksheet their teacher has brought.
programs.our_note: Sixty dollars for a whole class is the cheapest way in, and the clipboards mean you do not have to write anything yourself. Thirty students is a hard ceiling, so a big class needs splitting.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: There is no fee for extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers.
programs.evidence: Materials required for these activities are included in the Unguided Museum Visit fee of $60 per class (a maximum of 30 students).

programs.name: Group admission
programs.description: A group rate of $6 a person for any group of at least 8 people, giving the run of the galleries. Taxes are included in the posted admission prices. Children aged 5 and under are free.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the galleries at their own pace, looking at the collections from northern Vancouver Island.
programs.our_note: This is the route for a group that is not a K to 12 class, such as a daycare. It is per person rather than per group, so a party of twenty costs about a hundred and twenty dollars.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.

programs.name: Guided group tour
programs.description: A guided tour of the museum at $11 a person for groups of 10 or more. Advance booking is required and the museum asks that you book it by email.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide through the galleries and hear the stories behind the collections.
programs.our_note: This is the general group tour rather than a school program, and it costs more per head than the class rates. If your group is a K to 12 class, the flat class fees work out cheaper.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms and a picnic area on site, and the building is wheelchair accessible with a courtesy wheelchair to borrow. Whether there is somewhere indoors to eat and where a bus can pull in are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.evidence: Cost is $11/person for groups of 10 or more people.

images.alt: A long two storey building with a metal roof and tall glass windows, seen from above across a mown lawn ringed by conifers.
Five children stand in a row in front of a large black and red Northwest Coast design painted on a white wall, all looking and pointing upward.
A wooden fishing boat lettered Soyokaze sits on blocks under an open shelter beside a brick building.

gaps: PER CLASS INFERENCE: the museum states $60 per class only for the unguided visit, in the sheet that says 'the Unguided Museum Visit fee of $60 per class (a maximum of 30 students)'. The $100 guided fee is never labelled per class or per student. We have recorded it as a fee for the whole class because it sits beside the $60 class fee in the same list and on the same booking form. If it were per student, a class of 25 would be $2,500 rather than $100. Confirm it when you book.
The posted school fees are for the 2025-2026 school year, which has already ended, and no 2026-2027 fees are published. Prices may have changed.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: the full programme list, the free supervisor rule and the exact durations are on the booking request form at /learn/school-programs/educational-program-request-form/, not on the education programs page. Letters From The Front does not appear anywhere except that form.
Christmas Past is dated on the booking form as December 1 to 16, 2025, so the only published dates have passed. Assume you need to ask for this year's dates.

The Haig-Brown Property Guided Tour is at the Haig-Brown property, not at the museum building on Island Highway, and the museum does not publish that address, its washrooms, its parking or a wet weather plan.
No minimum notice period is published. The site says only that advance booking is required and that requests are handled in the order received.
No maximum group size is published for the guided programs. The 30 student cap is stated for the unguided visit only.
No adult to child ratio is published for any program. The booking form says only that extra adult supervisors and parent volunteers are free.

Whether a preschool or daycare group can book is not addressed. Every education program and the $60 unguided rate are written for grades K to 12, and the unguided sheet says that rate is only available for K-12 groups. A daycare group would fall back on the $6 per person group admission or the $11 per person guided tour.

Admission is listed as Adult $10, Senior $8, Student $6, Family $25 and free for children aged 5 and under. There is no band actually labelled child, so the child admission price has been left blank rather than guessed from the student rate.
Parking is free with the entrance off 5th Avenue, but nothing is published about whether a school bus can park or drop off there.
There is a picnic area on site, but nothing says whether there is anywhere indoors for a class to eat on a wet day.

The Kids Camps & Activities page returns no results in a browser as well as to a plain fetch. Its own page summary still describes summer camps from 2022, so there is nothing current there for a group.

IMAGE NOTE: the school programs photograph carries an empty alt attribute and the boat photograph is a CSS background rather than an image tag. Both alt texts were written after opening the image files and looking at them.
The home page Open Graph image is a visitor guide advertisement rather than a photograph, so the exterior photograph from the hours and admission page was used as the main image instead.

conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different grade ranges for the colonization program. One says grades 8 to 12 and the booking form says 6 to 12. If you have a grade 6 or 7 class, ask before you count on it.
They give two different grade ranges for the archaeology program, one starting at grade 7 and one at grade 6. A grade 6 class may or may not be eligible, so check when you book.
The Haig-Brown tour is described as two hours in one place and one hour in another. Plan your bus for the longer one and confirm the length when you book.
